title: Sole trader or limited company? How to choose
excerpt: It mostly comes down to how much you'll make and what you'll do with it. Here's how we work it out with new clients.
content:
It's the first question most new businesses ask us. There's no single answer, but there is a simple way to think about it.

Start simple

If you're testing an idea or earning a little on the side, start as a sole trader. It's quick and cheap to run.

When a company makes sense

Once your profit is well into five figures and you don't need all of it to live on, a company usually saves tax.

Ask us for the numbers

We'll show you both side by side, for your figures, on the free call.

title: Five tax dates every small business should know
excerpt: Miss one and the penalties start at once. Put these in your calendar now, or let us remind you.
content:
Most penalties we see come from simply missing a date. These are the five that matter most.

31 January

Personal tax returns, and the first payment on account.

Every quarter

VAT returns, one month and seven days after each quarter ends.

Nine months after year-end

Corporation tax is due, three months before the return.

title: How dental practices can save tax this year
excerpt: Equipment, associate pay and pensions: three places most practices leave money on the table.
content:
We look after forty practices, and the same three savings come up again and again.

Equipment

Chairs, scanners and X-ray machines can usually be claimed in full the year you buy them.

Associate pay

Getting the associate split right protects you if the tax office ever asks.

Pensions

Paying into a pension from the practice is one of the most tax-efficient things a principal can do.

title: CIS explained, for builders and their subcontractors
excerpt: What the Construction Industry Scheme is, who has to register and how to get your deductions back.
content:
If you work in building, the Construction Industry Scheme affects you, whether you hire or get hired.

If you hire subcontractors

You check each one, take tax off their pay, and file a return every month.

If you're a subcontractor

Tax is taken off your pay. Register properly and the rate drops from 30% to 20%.

Getting it back

Most subcontractors are owed some of it back at the end of the year. We claim it for you.
